subject: computer-science
title: Cyber Security: Stretch — CIA Triad
welcome_lead: Three letters underpin all security: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science stretch adventure on the CIA triad and security trade-offs.
final_note: You can now classify any attack or defence using the CIA framework.

concepts.def: Only authorised people can see the data.
Data is accurate and not tampered with.
Data is accessible when needed by users.
One-way transform used to check integrity.
A copy of data kept for recovery.
A fixed-length fingerprint of some data.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Confidentiality protects secrets (encryption, access control).

Integrity protects accuracy (hashing, checksums).

Availability keeps things online (backups, DoS protection).

• Phishing leaks passwords → Confidentiality
  • Tampering with a database row → Integrity
  • DoS flood → Availability
Run a file through SHA-256. If even one bit changes, the hash changes completely. Sites publish download hashes so you can verify the file wasn't tampered with.
